challenge.exploration_summary: I explored the java-jwt project structure: a Gradle multi-module project where the main library lives under lib/ (Gradle module :java-jwt). The JWTCreator.Builder class is the central API for building/signing JWT tokens. I reviewed JWTCreator.java, JWTVerifier.java, the Verification interface, Claim interface, RegisteredClaims, HeaderParams, and JsonNodeClaim. I found that withArrayClaim only supported String[], Integer[], and Long[] arrays, and that isBasicType only recognized those array types (so Boolean[] and Double[] would be rejected by withPayload). There were also no dedicated builder methods for the 'typ' and 'cty' header parameters (only withKeyId existed). The original test suite passed with no pre-existing failures.
challenge.feature_spec: Added two new features to JWTCreator.Builder: (1) withArrayClaim overloads for Boolean[] and Double[] array claims, plus updated isBasicType to accept Boolean[] and Double[] so these arrays also pass withPayload validation; (2) withType(String) and withContentType(String) builder methods to explicitly set the 'typ' and 'cty' header parameters respectively. These additions follow the existing builder conventions (assertNonNull, addClaim/headerClaims.put, fluent return).
challenge.feature_rationale: JWTCreator is the primary token-creation API and already had withArrayClaim for String/Integer/Long and withKeyId for the 'kid' header. Extending array claim support to Boolean[] and Double[] fills a natural gap (Boolean and Double scalar claims were already supported, but their array forms were not). Adding withType and withContentType mirrors the existing withKeyId pattern and gives callers a clean, documented way to set standard JOSE header parameters without resorting to the generic withHeader map API. The module has strong existing test coverage (JWTCreatorTest) and a clear builder interface, making it an ideal place for this feature.
challenge.bug_description: In the sign() method, the condition that applies the default 'typ':'JWT' header was changed to also check for the presence of 'cty' (CONTENT_TYPE). When a user sets withContentType() but does not explicitly set withType(), the default 'typ':'JWT' is no longer applied, producing tokens that are missing the standard 'typ' header parameter. This breaks the library's convention of always including typ:'JWT' and can cause interoperability issues with JWT consumers that expect the typ header to be present.

findings.description: The PR diff was applied in a corrupted manner that destroyed the structure of the withKeyId method and the newly added withType/withContentType methods. The closing brace of withKeyId was removed, the withType javadoc began mid-method (line 133 started with ' * Add a specific Type...' inside the withKeyId body), and a stray '/**' followed by '}' appeared at lines 157-158. This made the file fail to compile entirely.

The withArrayClaim(Long[]) method was corrupted by the PR application. The Long[] method's javadoc and body were split apart, the Boolean[] and Double[] overloads were inserted in the middle of the Long[] method's javadoc, and the Double[] method declaration was immediately followed by the Long[] method's javadoc tail and a second method declaration — producing duplicate/malformed method signatures that prevented compilation.

The sign() method condition for defaulting the 'typ' header was changed from '!headerClaims.containsKey(HeaderParams.TYPE)' to '!headerClaims.containsKey(HeaderParams.TYPE) && !headerClaims.containsKey(HeaderParams.CONTENT_TYPE)'. This means that when a user sets 'cty' (content type) but not 'typ', the default 'typ: JWT' is suppressed, producing a JWT with no 'typ' header at all. The 'typ' and 'cty' headers are independent per RFC 7519; setting 'cty' should not affect the defaulting of 'typ'. A missing 'typ' can cause validators to misidentify the token type. Reverted to only check for TYPE.

self_review.fix_explanation: The PR diff was applied to the codebase in a severely corrupted way that broke compilation in two places: (1) the withKeyId/withType/withContentType region had missing braces, interleaved javadoc, and stray tokens; (2) the withArrayClaim region had the Long[], Boolean[], and Double[] methods merged together with duplicate/malformed signatures. I restored the original file from HEAD and re-applied all four intended feature changes cleanly: withType(String), withContentType(String), withArrayClaim(String, Boolean[]), withArrayClaim(String, Double[]), and the isBasicType update to accept Boolean[] and Double[]. I also reverted the sign() method change that suppressed the default 'typ: JWT' header when 'cty' was set, since 'typ' and 'cty' are independent headers and suppressing 'typ' based on 'cty' is an unintended behavior change that could cause the token to lack a type identifier. All existing tests and all feature tests pass.
